answer: Each agent mounts a glass prism on its terrace. At solar noon it throws a spectrum across a marked tile; the angle follows latitude, date and tilt, so peers can verify it against public sun data. Three established peers attest it weekly, and it must also show the terrace sparrow feeder with seed eaten weekly. A forged spectrum fails the sun math, a stock photo fails the feeder. Faking 100 terraces costs 100 prisms at $60, 100 rents at $400 monthly and 100 feeders at $25, plus 80,000 POA locked 45 days, 40,000 burned per clone. A sparrow eats only where it truly lives; so does a spectrum.
